name: Overnight oats with banana & peanut butter
steps: The night before, mix oats, milk, chia seeds and honey in a jar.
Refrigerate overnight.
In the morning, slice the banana on top and swirl in the peanut butter.
tip: Oats + banana 1-2h before a run gives easily-digestible carbs without the fibre/fat overload that can cause GI issues mid-run.

name: Greek yogurt bowl with granola & berries
steps: Spoon yogurt into a bowl.
Top with granola and berries.
Drizzle with honey.
tip: Greek yogurt's protein-to-carb mix within 30-60 min post-run kickstarts muscle repair while topping up glycogen.

name: Scrambled eggs & avocado toast
steps: Toast the bread.
Whisk and scramble the eggs in olive oil over low heat.
Mash avocado onto toast, season.
Serve eggs and halved tomatoes alongside.
tip: Eggs are one of the few whole foods with a complete amino-acid profile — a solid recovery-day protein anchor after a hard training morning.

name: Banana & honey porridge
steps: Simmer oats in milk for 5 min, stirring.
Slice banana over the top.
Drizzle honey and dust with cinnamon.
tip: A high-carb, low-fat, low-fibre breakfast like this sits well in the stomach 1-3h before a long run or hard session.

name: Peanut butter & banana toast
steps: Toast the bread.
Spread peanut butter.
Top with sliced banana and a drizzle of honey.
tip: Quick and portable — a good option when you're fuelling less than an hour before heading out the door.

name: Spinach & feta omelette with oats
steps: Wilt spinach in a pan.
Whisk eggs, pour over spinach, crumble in feta.
Cook until set, fold.
Serve with a small side of plain oats.
tip: Pairing protein (eggs, feta) with a modest carb side supports both muscle repair and glycogen refill after a hard morning session.

name: French toast with berry compote
steps: Whisk eggs, milk and cinnamon.
Dip bread, pan-fry until golden both sides.
Simmer berries with honey for 3 min into a quick compote.
Serve toast topped with compote.
tip: A treat-y, higher-carb breakfast — good to place on a long-run morning where you'll burn through the extra energy.

name: Cottage cheese pancakes
steps: Blend cottage cheese, eggs and oat flour into a batter.
Cook small pancakes in a non-stick pan, 2 min per side.
Top with blueberries and maple syrup.
tip: Cottage cheese's slow-digesting casein protein makes this a good choice the morning after a heavy session, keeping amino acids trickling in for longer.

name: Chicken, rice & veg bowl
steps: Cook rice according to packet instructions.
Pan-fry sliced chicken breast until cooked through.
Steam broccoli and carrot.
Combine in a bowl, drizzle with soy sauce and oil.
tip: A balanced ~40/40/20 carb/protein/fat split like this is a solid default lunch on any training day, hard or easy.

name: Quinoa, chickpea & feta salad
steps: Cook quinoa per packet, cool slightly.
Combine with chickpeas, diced cucumber and halved tomatoes.
Crumble in feta.
Dress with olive oil and lemon juice.
tip: Chickpeas + quinoa together supply a fuller amino-acid profile than either alone — useful on plant-forward lunch days.

name: Tuna pasta salad
steps: Cook pasta, drain and cool.
Flake in tuna, add tomatoes, sweetcorn and thinly sliced onion.
Toss with olive oil.
tip: An easy make-ahead lunch to prep the night before a busy training day — tastes fine cold, no reheating needed.

name: Turkey & hummus wrap
steps: Spread hummus over the wrap.
Layer turkey, salad, carrot and cucumber.
Roll tightly and slice in half.
tip: A five-minute lunch is still a good lunch — consistency in eating enough day to day matters more than any single meal being perfect.

name: Lentil soup with crusty bread
steps: Sauté onion and carrot.
Add lentils and stock, simmer 20 min until soft.
Season with cumin, blend partially if you like it smoother.
Serve with bread.
tip: Lentils are a great budget source of both carbs and plant protein — good for a cheap, filling training-day lunch.

name: Salmon, sweet potato & greens
steps: Roast cubed sweet potato at 200°C for 20 min.
Pan-fry or bake salmon 8-10 min.
Steam green beans.
Plate together with a squeeze of lemon.
tip: Salmon's omega-3s have some evidence for reducing exercise-induced inflammation — a nice recovery-day protein choice.

name: Beef & vegetable stir-fry with noodles
steps: Cook noodles per packet.
Stir-fry beef in hot oil until browned, set aside.
Stir-fry vegetables with garlic and ginger.
Combine everything with noodles and soy sauce.
tip: Combining a decent protein hit with plenty of carbs covers both repair and glycogen refill in one plate — handy after a hard AM session.

name: Falafel pita with tahini
steps: Warm the falafel (oven or pan).
Slice open the pita.
Fill with salad, tomato, cucumber and falafel.
Drizzle with tahini.
tip: Chickpea-based falafel plus tahini gives a reasonable plant-protein lunch, though it runs lighter on protein than a meat/fish equivalent — pair with a protein-forward dinner.

name: Spaghetti bolognese
steps: Sauté onion and garlic in oil.
Brown the mince.
Add tomatoes and paste, simmer 20 min.
Cook spaghetti, combine and top with parmesan.
tip: A classic carb-loading dinner — eat this the night before a long run or hard interval session to top up glycogen stores.

name: Grilled chicken, roasted potatoes & broccoli
steps: Toss potato wedges in oil and paprika, roast 25 min at 200°C.
Grill or pan-fry chicken until cooked through.
Steam broccoli.
Plate together.
tip: High protein, moderate carb — a good choice on rest days or the evening after a hard session, when refuelling matters more than pre-loading.

name: Baked salmon, rice & asparagus
steps: Cook rice per packet.
Bake salmon at 200°C for 12-15 min with lemon and dill.
Steam or pan-grill asparagus.
Plate together.
tip: Fatty fish twice a week is a reasonable target for omega-3 intake — good to rotate in on lighter training days.

name: Vegetarian chili with rice
steps: Sauté onion and pepper.
Add beans, tomatoes and chili powder, simmer 20 min.
Cook rice separately.
Serve chili over rice.
tip: Beans deliver slow-release carbs plus fibre and plant protein — good the night before a long run, just not so close to it that the fibre causes GI discomfort mid-run.

name: Steak, sweet potato mash & green beans
steps: Boil and mash sweet potato with butter.
Pan-sear steak to preference.
Steam green beans.
Plate together, rest the steak 2-3 min before slicing.
tip: Red meat's iron is well-absorbed (heme iron) — worth keeping in rotation, since endurance runners run a higher risk of low iron stores.

name: Mushroom & parmesan risotto
steps: Sauté onion and mushrooms.
Add rice, toast briefly, deglaze with wine.
Add stock a ladle at a time, stirring, ~20 min.
Finish with butter and parmesan.
tip: Risotto's high carb density and low fibre make it easy on the stomach — a solid choice the evening before a long run.

name: Shrimp & vegetable stir-fry with rice noodles
steps: Soak rice noodles per packet.
Stir-fry shrimp until pink, set aside.
Stir-fry vegetables and garlic.
Combine everything with noodles and soy sauce.
tip: Lighter and lower-fat than a red-meat dinner, so it digests faster — useful if your long run is first thing the next morning.

name: Turkey meatballs with pasta
steps: Mix turkey mince with breadcrumbs and egg, form meatballs.
Pan-fry until browned, then simmer in passata with garlic for 10 min.
Cook pasta.
Combine and top with basil.
tip: Turkey mince keeps this leaner than beef while still hitting a solid protein number alongside the carb-loading pasta base.

name: Banana with peanut butter
steps: Slice the banana.
Serve with peanut butter for dipping (or spread on top).
tip: A simple, fast-digesting pre-run snack — good 30-60 min before heading out.

name: Rice cakes with honey
steps: Drizzle honey over the rice cakes.
tip: Low fat, low fibre, high carb — about as gentle on the stomach as a pre-run snack gets.

name: Greek yogurt with honey
steps: Stir honey into the yogurt.
tip: A quick protein top-up if your next full meal is more than an hour or two after training.

name: Protein shake with banana
steps: Blend all ingredients until smooth.
tip: Convenient when appetite is low right after a hard effort but you still want protein in within that first hour or two.

name: Almonds & dried apricots
steps: Combine in a small bowl or bag.
tip: A good grab-and-go option for an easy or rest day when you don't need to fuel specifically around a session.

name: Dates stuffed with almond butter
steps: Slit each date open and remove the pit.
Fill with almond butter.
tip: Dates are one of the most concentrated natural sources of fast carbs — a favourite among endurance athletes for exactly that reason.

name: Cottage cheese with pineapple
steps: Combine cottage cheese and pineapple in a bowl.
tip: A genuinely good protein/carb recovery snack, whatever you make of the (thin) evidence around pineapple's anti-inflammatory effects.

name: Oat & cocoa energy balls
steps: Mix all ingredients into a thick dough.
Roll into 6 small balls.
Refrigerate 20 min before eating (batch keeps all week).
tip: Batch these once and you've got a pre-run snack ready to grab all week — no need to remember to prep one each morning.
